submitter: bugs_open/386 session — Go slice (fact-value history: the register remembers the readings it actually held)
rationale:
bugs_open/386: the daily evidence-freshness refresh overwrites a counting fact's value and DISCARDS the reading it just held (refresh_evidence_base_action.go:534-544). Every already-deployed page rendering the previous value is then convicted by numberSupported as an unregistered_number at ERROR severity (validate_page_content.go:1324-1326; error is failing at :420 and returns without saving at :449) — so a page whose only fault is being a day old cannot be rebuilt to fix itself, and in the bugs_open/033 review queue it is indistinguishable from a real fabrication. It re-arms nightly with nobody doing anything wrong.

The fix teaches the register to remember: for a fact a human has ARMED, the refresh appends the outgoing {value, verified_at} before overwriting, and numberSupported treats an EXACT match against a retained reading — inside the same context-term gate as today — as supported. A page that published a figure while the register held it did not invent that figure.

WHY THIS SHAPE AND NOT THE BUG FILE'S OWN CANDIDATE 1. That candidate proposed a monotonic flag and a range [previous, current]. Both are wrong here, measured rather than argued: 8 of 29 sql-sourced number facts have FALLEN at least once (aao-orchestrations 17 falls / 34 transitions, C4-orchestration-state-records 17/38 ranging 1,625-90,790), so a monotonic flag would encode a false premise into the schema; and a range vouches for every intermediate value nobody ever published. Exact-match-against-retained-readings is strictly tighter, needs no monotonicity assumption, and can never accept a number the register did not carry.

WHY THE OWNER'S RULING DOES NOT COVER THIS CASE. The owner ruled 2026-08-25 (bug file §4b, commit 2a9091c7d) that a counting fact should be expressed as 'at least N' or the claim cancelled. That is right and this change does not touch it — but it cannot reach this bug's motivating case, and §4b explicitly preserves candidate 1 for that reason. The five facts convicting fundamentallyai's page (F9-F13) have NO writer_line, so they contribute nothing to composeWriterBlock: their numbers reach the page through an evidence-chart component rendering the register into content_data, not through prose. There is no sentence to rephrase, only a chart — and the chart stamps its own 'verified 2026-08-23', so 'Feed items collected 11513 verified 2026-08-23' is a TRUE statement for ever. The register simply cannot currently agree with it.

THE PREMISE IS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. 'Every stale rendered value was once the register's current value' is what the design rests on, and it was disconfirmable — a rounded or paraphrased figure would have matched nothing. cmd/claimscan over 91 components (export asserted 91 vs 91 in the DB, stderr empty, 4-column recipe with page_type) returns exactly 5 findings, all on capabilities/evidence-chart. All 5 values — 11513, 10194, 428, 483, 23 — were the register's own value on 2026-08-23, the day the component was written at 17:26, and none is current. 5 of 5.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT FIX, stated so no reviewer has to find it: a FALLING lower-bound claim. A gte fact whose rate dips below a published floor ('over 1,600 orchestrations a day' when today's rate is 1,494) is not rescued, because history is exact-only and 1,600 was never a retained reading. Applying the tolerance to history instead would pin support at the all-time maximum for ever — after one busy day, 'over 7,000 a day' would be vouched for on every quiet day thereafter — which is the accidental-support gradient of bugs_open/364 §2 with time as the amplifier, and strictly worse than today's behaviour. That class belongs to the owner's ruling with the floor set below the historic LOW, not to this mechanism.

plan.summary: An opt-in, capped, exact-match memory of a fact's superseded readings: two typed fields plus one reader on EvidenceFact, and one writer in the refresh that records the outgoing value before the overwrite. Default OFF; a fact is armed by a human, per fact, in the register. No behaviour changes for any fact nobody arms.

edits.rationale: Two optional fields on the fact plus the entry type and the cap. RetainHistory governs BOTH halves (writer records only for an armed fact; reader consults only for one), so a History array present without the flag is inert by design — seeding one must not widen support on its own. History is a DISTINCT field from Observations rather than a reuse of it, because IsSeries() keys on len(Observations) (claims_series.go:82-84) and reusing that slot would silently turn every armed fact into a series and route it down the series branch of numberSupported. FactHistoryEntry deliberately carries no per-entry Source, unlike Observation: an observation is an independent assertion that must prove itself, whereas a history entry records what THIS register previously held, whose provenance is the parent fact's source plus the date — inventing a per-entry source would imply an attestation nobody made. Both fields carry omitempty so the ~295 unarmed facts in the fleet serialise byte-identically.
edits.sketch:
RetainHistory bool `json:"retain_history,omitempty"`
History []FactHistoryEntry `json:"history,omitempty"`

type FactHistoryEntry struct {
	Value      float64 `json:"value"`
	VerifiedAt string  `json:"verified_at"`
}

const FactHistoryMaxEntries = 90 // ~3 months at the daily refresh cadence measured 2026-08-25

edits.rationale: The new arm sits INSIDE the existing context-term gate and after the tolerance switch, so a retained reading is only ever evidence for the claim the fact scopes — one armed counter must not start vouching for unrelated figures elsewhere on the page. Exact-only, deliberately: a former reading is one specific number the register held, never a range, so unlike a tolerance it cannot vouch for a value the register never carried. The cap is enforced at the READER as well as the writer, because the cap bounds what the scan ACCEPTS and a guard living only in the writer is not a bound — a hand seed or a migration backfill can produce an over-cap array.

edits.symbol: recordFactHistory, siteRefreshResult.FactsHistoryRecorded, the sql refresh arm
edits.rationale: Records the outgoing reading BEFORE the overwrite, because after it the value is unrecoverable from this map. Operates on the RAW map, never a typed round-trip: this action works on map[string]interface{} precisely so unknown keys survive the rewrite (its own comment: 'this action must never drop a human's data'), and marshalling one fact through EvidenceFact to add two fields would drop every key the struct does not model. Four refusals, each closing a way this could quietly widen what the scan accepts: unarmed facts skipped; no outgoing value records nothing (writing a zero would invent a reading); a repeat of the newest entry is not appended, so a second refresh on one day cannot inflate the history (measured: 2026-08-16 carries two refreshes); the array is trimmed from the FRONT so the oldest goes, since the newest readings are the ones a still-stale page is likely carrying. FactsHistoryRecorded is reported separately from FactsUpdated because they can legitimately disagree — an unarmed fact moving increments only the latter, so a run showing updates and zero history is the honest signal that nothing is armed yet rather than a silent failure of retention.

Every fixture is MINIMAL — one fact, and where a negative is asserted, nothing else in the register that could support the value for an unrelated reason. That is not style: the bugs_open/364 lane's first draft used a populated register and PASSED with its own fix reverted, because another fact was quietly supporting the number. So each positive is paired with the same fixture mutated at exactly one point asserting the opposite outcome — armed/unarmed, in-window/out-of-window, at-cap/over-cap. The four reader guards were mutation-proved in an isolated git worktree (history arm deleted; reader opt-in gate dropped; reader cap dropped; history hoisted above the context gate) and every mutation KILLED its named test.
edits.sketch:
TestHistorySupportsAFormerReading / TestHistoryIsInertWhenNotArmed (the mutation pair)
TestHistoryDoesNotBecomeBlanketSupport — 11512, 11514, 11600, 11647 all refused
TestHistoryStaysInsideTheContextTermGate — with an in-window control so the negative is the gate, not a break
TestHistoryDoesNotMakeAFactASeries — the Observations field-collision guard
TestHistoryCapIsEnforcedAtTheReader — oldest refused, newest and boundary accepted
TestHistoryRoundTripsThroughJSON — omitempty proven, so unarmed facts serialise byte-identically

edits.rationale: Asserts on the RAW MAP, not a typed struct, because that is what the action mutates and the map is what can lose data. TestHistoryPreservesUnknownFactKeys is the no-data-loss guard and is the one to keep if these are ever pruned. TestRecordFactHistoryWrittenEntriesAreReadableByTheScanner closes the loop — the writer's raw-map output must parse into the typed fact the scan consumes, so a key-name mismatch cannot pass both halves separately. The three writer guards were mutation-proved in an isolated worktree (opt-in gate dropped; duplicate guard dropped; trim direction inverted) and every mutation KILLED its named test. Both full packages then passed fresh with -count=1, including the 364 lane's concurrent surface tests.
edits.sketch:
TestRecordFactHistoryAppendsTheOutgoingReading
TestRecordFactHistoryIgnoresUnarmedFacts — asserts the KEY is absent, not an empty array
TestRecordFactHistoryNeedsAnOutgoingValue — a nil outgoing must not write a zero
TestRecordFactHistoryDoesNotDuplicateTheNewestReading — two refreshes on 2026-08-16 are real
TestRecordFactHistoryTrimsFromTheFront
TestHistoryPreservesUnknownFactKeys / TestRecordFactHistoryWrittenEntriesAreReadableByTheScanner

grounded_in: refresh_evidence_base_action.go:534-544 — 'if entry.Outcome != "fresh" { fact["value"] = live; fact["verified_at"] = today ... }'. The previous reading is not kept anywhere in the fact. This is the defect, read end to end.

refresh_evidence_base_action.go:317-323 — 'Work on the generic map so unknown keys ... survive the rewrite untouched — this action must never drop a human's data.' Both register writers marshal the raw map (refresh:1278, evidence_citations:350, the latter confirmed map-typed at :225), so new fact keys round-trip and no typed marshal-back exists to drop them.

validate_page_content.go:1324-1326 files unregistered_number at Severity 'error'; :420 computes validity as blocker==0 && error==0; :449 returns an error without saving. So 'error refuses the rebuild' is confirmed at the code, against the softer in-code comment nearby.
claims_series.go:82-84 — IsSeries() returns true when len(Observations) > 0. This is why History is a distinct field: reusing Observations would flip every armed fact into a series.

MEASURED 2026-08-25: cmd/claimscan over fundamentallyai (91 components, export asserted 91 vs count(*), stderr 0 bytes, page_type column supplied) → exactly 5 findings, all capabilities/evidence-chart. All 5 values (11513, 10194, 428, 483, 23) were the register's value on 2026-08-23, the day the component was written (17:26); none is current. The premise holds 5 of 5 and could have failed.

MEASURED 2026-08-25: 8 of 29 sql-sourced number facts have fallen at least once — aao-orchestrations 17 falls/34 transitions (1,494-7,281), C4-orchestration-state-records 17/38 (1,625-90,790), aao-work-items 12/34 (1,051-7,816). So the bug file's own 'monotonic' primitive would encode a false premise. Independently corroborated by 218_evidence_facts_for_043_sites.sql:48, written 2026-07-24: 'work items completed is NOT MONOTONIC: 1,267 on 07-24, 1,051 today'.

MEASURED 2026-08-25: the fact history is reconstructible today — 315 superseded evidence_base spec rows across 15 sites back to 2026-07-16, because the refresh supersedes rather than overwrites (refresh_evidence_base_action.go:1289-1318). fundamentallyai's F9 reconstructs daily and 11513 is present, dated 2026-08-23. So the Phase 2 backfill has a real source and is not guesswork.

MEASURED 2026-08-25, the zero-consumer enumeration this scope argument requires rather than asserts: SELECT count(*) FROM site_specs, LATERAL jsonb_array_elements(data->'facts') f WHERE aspect='evidence_base' AND is_current AND (f ? 'retain_history' OR f ? 'history') → 0. No live consumer names either key.

Consumers told, per the 2026-07-29 §3 ruling. numberSupported has exactly 2 non-test call sites — claims.go:916 (ScanUnregisteredNumbers) and claims_stats.go:327 (ScanStatClaims) — reaching the build gate (validate_page_content.go:1322), both discovery checks (check_unverified_claims.go:621, check_unverified_claims_stats.go:120), the save floor (save_sections_claims_guard.go) and cmd/claimscan. Two further servers expose the raw facts array and will carry the new keys in their payloads: internal/core-manager/handlers/sitefacts.go:97-104 (payload grows; the cap bounds it) and tool_backend_provision.go (counts entries; per-fact keys do not change the count). What changes for all of them is the same one sentence: an ARMED fact now also accepts values the register previously held, exactly, within its existing context terms.

OWNER RULING 2026-08-25, bug file §4b (commit 2a9091c7d): a counting fact is expressed as 'at least' N or the claim is cancelled — and §4b explicitly states candidate 1 'remains the durable fix and is not superseded by this ruling'. This change is that candidate, re-shaped by the falling-counter measurement above.
plan.risks:
1. FALSE-NEGATIVE SURFACE, and it is real: an invented number that EXACTLY equals a retained former value, in a window matching the fact's context terms, is now vouched for. For 5-digit counters the collision odds are negligible; for small ones ('23 vetoes') they are not. Three things bound it — arming is a per-fact human act in the register, the context-term gate still applies unchanged, and the 90-entry cap keeps the accepted set small and reviewable. Before ARMING any fact the author owes the offline control: diff cmd/claimscan findings baseline vs armed over the whole site and read every finding that disappears in >=300 chars of context. Anything beyond the known stale-render set means the terms are too broad. That control is Phase 2's gate, not this slice's, because this slice arms nothing.

2. THIS SLICE IS INERT ON ARRIVAL. Zero facts carry retain_history (query above), so rolling it changes no verdict anywhere. That is the intended posture per the 2026-08-02 §2 ruling — new authority on a shared seam ships as an opt-in field with the unsafe default OFF — but it also means the mechanism cannot be proven by a green fleet: a post-roll run showing zero findings-changed is expected and is NOT evidence it works. The honest proof is the paired armed/unarmed claimscan run named in the tests, plus FactsHistoryRecorded becoming non-zero after Phase 2 arms a fact and the next refresh tick moves it.

3. CAP CHOICE. 90 entries is ~3 months at the daily cadence measured 2026-08-25. Too small and a genuinely stale page falls outside the window and stays convicted; too large and the accepted set grows without bound. It is a judgement, stated as one. It is enforced at both ends so neither side can be the only guard.

4. CONCURRENCY, disclosed. The 364 lane committed two changes to claims.go today (52958897f, fa0b513f1) which are NOT yet rolled, so the fleet runs page-grain while HEAD runs component-grain. I checked before designing: those edits are confined to ClaimSurface / ProseNumbersAreClaims / the surface maps and threading, and touch none of numberSupported, ContextTerms, Tolerance or seriesSupports. No semantic overlap with this slice. But two sessions in one file means a same-file passenger no pathspec can exclude, so this slice is deliberately confined to the fact-matching path.

5. WHAT THIS DOES NOT FIX, restated as a limitation rather than left to be discovered: a falling lower-bound claim (see rationale). Exact-only is the choice that makes history safe, and it is also the choice that leaves that class alone. It belongs to the owner's ruling with the floor set below the historic LOW — measured per fact, since 8 of 29 facts fall.
